concepts.def: Sticking your attention on one thing
Ignoring all but the chosen input
Trying to do two things at once
Hearing your name in a noisy room

walkthroughs.body_html:
Your senses gather way more data than the brain can use.

Attention picks what matters now.

At a noisy party you can focus on one chat. That's selective attention.

Then if someone across the room says your name, your brain snaps over. That's the cocktail party effect. 🎉

The brain doesn't do two thinking tasks at once.

It rapidly switches — and each switch costs time and accuracy.

Homework and phone? You'll take 2x longer and learn less. ⏳
